parsed.attack: Nobody but the user ever installs: the parent on the other end receives a phone call, which is the entire value delivered, with zero software involved. So community_embed here means the founder posting once on Show HN or r/productivity - a spike, not a loop - and there is nothing to sustain it, because the product deliberately produces no artifact, no shared state, and nothing anyone would say out loud, since 'an app reminded me to ring my mother' is a confession rather than a recommendation. That is exactly the shape of UpHabit, which closed in April 2026 while saying the product worked, and of Donna, Humin and Refresh before it: good products with a referral coefficient of zero.
parsed.strongest_defence: The audience is enormous and self-identifying - every HN thread about someone's home-made last-contact tracker reaches the front page - so one post plus a standing presence in r/AgingParents can carry the first few thousand installs for nothing, after which conversion funds the rest.
parsed.verdict_reason: The first spike is free but the coefficient after it is zero, so sustained growth reverts to $20-80 paid installs against $8-24 per payer.
